stories.title: Israel election: no clear winner for Netanyahu
stories.body: Israelis voted on 27 October with 77.7 percent turnout, the highest since 1999. Exit polls gave Prime Minister Netanyahu's bloc about 51–52 seats against about 49–51 for the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party. Likud is projected to be the largest party with about 27 seats. A government needs 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats. President Isaac Herzog will nominate a candidate, who then has up to 42 days to form a government; until then Netanyahu stays on as caretaker.
stories.why: Who governs Israel shapes the Gaza ceasefire and the war with Iran, both live interview topics.

cards.front: How many seats are in Israel's Knesset, and how many are needed for a majority?
Who led the main opposition bloc in Israel's October 2026 election?
cards.back: Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party.

stories.title: Iran and Qatar leaders meet at gas summit in Moscow
stories.body: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian met Qatar's Emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, at the 8th Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit in Moscow. They discussed energy cooperation and wider ties. Qatar is mediating between Iran and the US and has sent a delegation to Tehran, but its foreign ministry also called on Iran to stop threatening Gulf states. The war is now nearly eight months old.
stories.why: Nigeria is a member of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum, and the war's effect on gas markets matters for Nigerian LNG.

cards.front: Where was the 8th Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit held in October 2026?

stories.title: Hunters fight off bandits in Katsina
stories.body: Katsina State authorities said local hunters killed 14 suspected bandits who attacked travellers in Bakori LGA on 23 October. A traveller was burnt in his vehicle and one hunter was killed. Officials said the attackers, about 26 men on 13 motorcycles, were heading towards Dawan Laila forest. The state warned of possible reprisals; Premium Times could not independently verify the figures.
stories.why: Communities arming themselves is a sign of how stretched formal security is in the North-west, and it raises the risk of reprisal violence.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine and US to meet in Abu Dhabi in November
stories.body: The Kremlin said three-way talks are planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi. Putin wants talks on long-term security arrangements rather than a short truce, and Russia still demands territory and no NATO membership for Ukraine. Zelenskyy wants strong security guarantees, ten years of funding for Ukraine's army and European involvement. Both sides exchanged 270 prisoners of war, and Ukraine says more than 19,000 civilians have been killed since 2022.
stories.why: A settlement would shift world grain and fuel prices that feed Nigerian inflation.

cards.front: When and where are US–Russia–Ukraine talks planned (as of late October 2026)?
cards.back: The first half of November 2026, in Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: Iran blames US as fears of new strikes grow
stories.body: President Masoud Pezeshkian blamed Washington for the collapse of an interim deal to end the war and said both sides should return to it. President Trump said he "may do another little Epic Fury", the codename of the US–Israeli campaign that began on 28 February. The Revolutionary Guards warned that even limited strikes would bring a response several times greater. Iran's Supreme Leader is now Mojtaba Khamenei, who succeeded his father and has not been seen in public since early March.
stories.why: A return to full-scale strikes would push oil and shipping costs even higher for Nigeria.

cards.front: What is the codename of the US–Israeli war on Iran that began on 28 February 2026?

stories.title: Former DSS chief Bichi to chair the National Institute for Security Studies
stories.body: President Tinubu approved Yusuf Magaji Bichi, the immediate past Director-General of the DSS, as chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS) in Abuja. He serves an initial four-year term from 22 October 2026 and succeeds A.A. Gadzama. The appointment was recommended by the current DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Ajayi.
stories.why: NISS trains officers across Nigeria's security and intelligence community, so its leadership is a fair general-knowledge question.

cards.front: Who chairs the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (as of October 2026)?
cards.back: Yusuf Magaji Bichi, former Director-General of the DSS.
